subject: science
skillName: Fair Tests to Improve a Design

items.prompt:
In a fair test you change
A) everything at once
B) only one variable at a time
C) nothing
D) the results
items.answer: B) only one variable at a time

steps: Changing one variable keeps the test fair.

items.prompt:
A place where a design does not work well or breaks is a
A) criterion
B) failure point
C) constraint
D) reward

steps: Failure points show what to improve.

items.prompt:
Why keep other things the same in a fair test?
A) To make it harder
B) So any difference comes from the one change
C) To change the result
D) It does not matter
items.answer: B) So any difference comes from the one change

steps: Controlled variables reveal the true cause.

items.prompt:
A toy bridge keeps cracking in the middle. Engineers should
A) ignore it
B) strengthen the middle and test again
C) stop testing
D) make it longer only
items.answer: B) strengthen the middle and test again

steps: The middle is a failure point to improve and retest.

items.prompt:
A model or first version of a design that is tested is called a
A) prototype
B) constraint
C) criterion
D) graph

steps: A prototype is built to be tested and improved.

items.prompt:
A student changes a boat's shape AND material at once and it floats better. The problem is
A) nothing, it is a fair test
B) you cannot tell which change caused the improvement
C) the boat is too big
D) there were no variables
items.answer: B) you cannot tell which change caused the improvement

steps: Two changes at once make the cause unclear.

items.prompt:
To fairly test if a heavier weight makes a car roll farther, you should
A) change the weight and the ramp
B) change only the weight and keep the ramp, car, and start the same
C) change the car and the weight
D) change nothing
items.answer: B) change only the weight and keep the ramp, car, and start the same

steps: Only the weight should differ to see its effect.

items.prompt:
Why are fair-test results more trustworthy?
A) They take longer
B) Only one variable changed, so the cause of the result is clear
C) They use more materials
D) They skip measuring
items.answer: B) Only one variable changed, so the cause of the result is clear

steps: Controlling variables makes the cause certain.
